anti_averaging_principle: A category's hard_gates are pass/fail conditions that cannot be offset by strength elsewhere. The overall weighted score is informative, but a data factory run is only 'ready' when (a) the weighted average >= overall_completeness_threshold, (b) every category's own score >= its own completeness_threshold, and (c) every category's hard_gates all pass. This mirrors language already in this branch's docs/data/telecom-sector.md: 'the engine must not label the sector ready before the weighted score and all hard gates pass.'

hard_gates.condition: company_model completeness < 60%
hard_gates.action: category is treated as failing regardless of governance_profile/industry_context scores; a company record cannot be usable without a minimally identified issuer

applicability.description: Every company has an identity, a governance structure and an industry context. No sector pack may mark this category not_applicable in whole; only individual fields within it (e.g. sharia_status for a non-Saudi cross-listed issuer) may be narrowed by a sector/company pack flag.

hard_gates.condition: fewer than 5 audited annual periods OR fewer than 12 trailing quarterly periods ingested
hard_gates.action: category is capped at not-ready regardless of per-field completeness, matching the project's existing five-annual/12-quarter readiness gate described in docs/data/telecom-sector.md

hard_gates.condition: any statement value is present without a matching source_documents/content_hash row
hard_gates.action: value is rejected at validation, never published — no synthetic or derived-without-declared-formula statement values are allowed (project rule, see docs/data/known-data-regressions-cleanup.md and telecom-sector.md 'no-synthetic-source' gate)

applicability.description: Every listed company files financial statements. financial_notes sub-items (e.g. segment note detail) may be narrowed by whether that note class exists for the company (e.g. no lease_maturity_by_band if the company has no leases), which is a per-field not_applicable, not a category-level exemption.

hard_gates.condition: a ratio is populated but one or more of its declared formula inputs is itself unavailable/not_applicable
hard_gates.action: publish is rejected; the ratio must be marked missing_formula_inputs_or_history instead of silently computed from a substituted or estimated input (no filling gaps to make a derived number look complete)

provenance_requirements.calculated_field_supplement: Instead of a document_hash, a calculated field must carry a formula_id (a versioned identifier for the exact formula used) plus the field_key/period of every input it consumed, so the number is reproducible without re-deriving provenance by hand.

applicability.condition: financial_statements category has enough inputs populated to compute the formula; for banking/insurance issuers, the sector pack's own ratio set (see sector-specific_fields) takes precedence and the corresponding generic ratio may be not_applicable
applicability.description: Applicable to every company by default. A sector pack may declare that a specific generic ratio is superseded by a sector-specific equivalent (e.g. a bank's net_interest_margin supersedes the generic gross_margin concept for that line), in which case the generic field is not_applicable for that sector, not unavailable.

hard_gates.condition: relative valuation multiples (price_to_earnings, price_to_book, ev_ebitda) are below 90% even though market_data and financial_statements are both above their own thresholds
hard_gates.action: category fails regardless of the consensus sub-group's score, since consensus is the one part of this category this project has already accepted as structurally hard to close for free

provenance_requirements.calculated_field_supplement: Relative-valuation fields carry a formula_id like the other derived categories. Consensus fields, when populated, must carry the vendor/publication name and date as source_url-equivalent attribution per docs/SOURCE_MAP.md's Opinion/Secondary tier rule (always attributed, never promoted to a primary fact).

applicability.condition: the 'valuation' field_group is always applicable once market_data and financial_statements exist; the 'consensus' field_group is only applicable if the company has attributable analyst coverage at all (many Nomu-listed and small-cap issuers have none, which is not_applicable rather than unavailable)
applicability.description: Relative valuation multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, etc.) are internally computed and always applicable. Consensus-estimate fields require the company to actually have third-party coverage; absence of coverage is a structural fact about the company, not a missing extraction.

hard_gates.condition: no market_data value has been retrieved from exchange_market_data_feed in the last 5 trading days for an actively listed company
hard_gates.action: category is flagged failing even if historical depth is otherwise strong; stale live price data cannot be averaged away by good historical coverage

applicability.description: Applies to every actively listed company. A delisted or suspended company's market_data becomes not_applicable going forward (it still keeps its historical values) once the sector/company pack's listing_status flag changes.

hard_gates.condition: a dividend_per_share or payout figure is populated with no matching corporate_actions/disclosures announcement id
hard_gates.action: rejected at validation; dividend facts must trace to an actual announcement, never be inferred from a price change alone

applicability.condition: applicable to every company; a company that has never declared a dividend has an empty-but-valid history, which is event_not_observed, not unavailable
applicability.description: Every company is eligible to pay dividends, so the category itself is always applicable; individual history fields for a non-paying company are not_applicable via event_not_observed rather than unavailable, so a young or growth-stage issuer is not penalized for having no dividend to report.

hard_gates.condition: company_pack.reports_multiple_segments is true (multi-segment) AND segment_revenue is missing for any disclosed segment
hard_gates.action: category fails outright; a multi-segment company cannot be treated as complete while silently dropping one segment's revenue line

applicability.condition: applicable only if the company reports more than one operating segment under its accounting standard; a genuinely single-business-line company has this category marked not_applicable at the company level, evidenced by the operating-segments note itself stating there is one reportable segment
applicability.description: This is the canonical example the task description calls out: 'Segments may not apply to a single-business-line company'. The flag is data-driven — it must cite the note in the audited statements that states the segment count, not an assumption from the sector.

hard_gates.condition: sum of disclosed ownership_percentage across all holder rows for a period exceeds 100% or, once free_float is added, is inconsistent with it
hard_gates.action: rejected at validation; ownership must reconcile arithmetically, matching the project's existing practice of publishing ownership only when positions reconcile to 100% (docs/data/telecom-sector.md)

applicability.condition: always applicable; the named-institutional-holder breakdown (e.g. identifying Vanguard/BlackRock by name rather than an ownership_percentage aggregate) is the one sub-field this project has already flagged as requiring a licensed/attributed vendor (docs/SOURCE_MAP.md category 4)
applicability.description: Applies to every company. The free/official disclosure covers holder percentages ≥5%, free float and foreign ownership; granular named-institutional-holder detail is the licensed exception, tracked explicitly rather than silently folded into the free majority of the category.

hard_gates.condition: a corporate action fact exists with no announcement_id linking it to a disclosures record
hard_gates.action: rejected; every action must trace to the announcement that declared it

applicability.condition: always_applicable; an individual action type (e.g. stock_split) with no historical occurrence is event_not_observed
applicability.description: Every listed company is eligible for every corporate action type; a specific action never having happened is a fact about the company's history, not a gap.

hard_gates.condition: no announcement captured for an actively listed company in the trailing 180 days
hard_gates.action: flagged failing regardless of historical density, since a live issuer that stops appearing in the feed is far more likely to indicate a broken connector than a genuinely silent company

applicability.description: Every listed company publishes exchange/issuer announcements. This category is measured as polling coverage over a rolling window, not as a fixed field checklist, because new announcements are an open-ended, continuously arriving stream rather than a fill-once set of fields.

hard_gates.condition: the sector pack activates a field_group for this company but zero fields in it are populated across the trailing 4 quarters
hard_gates.action: category fails outright for that company even if other activated field_groups are strong, so one entirely-empty activated KPI group cannot be averaged away by a well-covered one

applicability.condition: a company is assigned exactly the operational KPI field_groups its sector pack activates (e.g. telecommunications for a telecom operator); every other field_group in this category is not_applicable for that company by construction, not by exception
applicability.description: This category holds physical/operating-unit metrics (subscriber counts, occupancy, production volumes, store counts, bed counts, AUM) as distinct from category 16's sector-specific financial-statement-shaped lines and ratios — see docs/architecture/data-factory-18-categories.md for the explicit dividing rule between the two, since catalog.py itself does not separate them within a single industry field_group.

hard_gates.condition: sector_pack activates this category for a company and its score is materially near zero while financial_statements and profitability both pass their own thresholds
hard_gates.action: overall readiness cannot be labeled ready; this is the contract's direct implementation of the anti-averaging principle named in the task ('a whole category cannot be near-zero even if others are strong'), and mirrors the existing project rule in docs/data/telecom-sector.md that 'the engine must not label the sector ready before the weighted score and all hard gates pass'

applicability.condition: a company is assigned exactly the sector-specific financial-statement-shaped field_groups its sector pack activates (e.g. banking for a bank); this is the category the task description's 'Banking-Specific' example maps to
applicability.description: Holds sector-specific balance-sheet/income/ratio lines that replace or supplement the universal financial_statements/profitability categories for a given sector (gross_loans, net_interest_margin for banks; loss_ratio, combined_ratio for insurers; FFO/NAV for REITs) — distinct from category 15's physical operating-unit KPIs.

hard_gates.condition: a composite score (piotroski_f_score, altman_z_score, beneish_m_score) is populated while one of its declared component sub-scores is marked unavailable
hard_gates.action: rejected; a composite score can never be computed from a partial input set with the gap silently zero-filled — it must be marked missing_formula_inputs_or_history as a whole instead

provenance_requirements.calculated_field_supplement: Every field in this category must carry a formula_id and its full list of consumed input field_key/period pairs — this is the category where 'no AI/LLM as a source' matters most operationally, since a formula_id must resolve to a declared, versioned, human-authored formula in the codebase, never to an LLM-estimated number.

applicability.condition: applicable whenever the underlying financial_statements/market_data inputs a given metric needs are themselves populated; a metric needing a longer history than the company has listed (e.g. a 10-year CAGR) is not_applicable for that company, not unavailable
applicability.description: Composite/smart scores (Piotroski F-score, Altman Z-score, Beneish M-score, accrual ratio) and long-window analytics (10y CAGRs, total returns, moving averages). All are internally computed, never fetched.

hard_gates.condition: any published fact anywhere in the dataset is missing one of its own category's provenance_requirements.mandatory_fields
hard_gates.action: that fact is excluded from its category's completeness numerator entirely (it does not count as populated) until the missing provenance is supplied — this is the single hard gate that enforces every other category's provenance_requirements block

hard_gates.condition: any published fact's age exceeds its own category's freshness_policy.max_age_before_stale_days
hard_gates.action: the fact is flagged stale and excluded from the 'currently fresh' completeness numerator, even though it remains visible as historical data with its staleness disclosed

applicability.condition: applies to every fact in every other category; this category's own score is not measured over a distinct field list but over the provenance completeness of all other categories' populated facts
applicability.description: Not a content category like 1-17. It is the audit layer: for every fact published anywhere in the contract, did it carry the provenance_requirements its own category mandates, and is it within its own category's freshness_policy. This category exists so provenance/freshness is scored and gated explicitly rather than assumed.
